checked.claim: A ruling card that finds nothing to rule on (item handed over, character deleted, ask the primary no longer holds) hands its buttons back and says nothing on screen
checked.why: ruleItemWorksOrItemNoEffectOrItemRefuse reads the item before the itemRefuse branch and returns null when it is gone (messenger-app.mjs:938-941), so Refuse cannot settle either; claimCard drops the claim on a null outcome and says nothing (bridge-asks.mjs:1337-1343); wireCallActions then re-enables the buttons with no notification (messenger-app.mjs:766-783). transferItem deletes the last piece (inventory.mjs:1199). The creative-use card is posted by promptAndCallGm with no expires (use-items.mjs:595-610; call-gm.mjs:1306), so sweepAskCards (call-gm.mjs:207-216, askCardExpiry null -> continue) never ends it. For a Call's Approve, answerHopeCall answers false when yesOnPrimary holds no ask (bridge-asks.mjs:708-713; call-gm.mjs:476-484), and yesOnPrimary's only word is warn() - console.warn plus the session log (utils.mjs:333-336), on the primary's browser. Refuse of a Call always answers true (bridge-asks.mjs:715-718), so that half is Approve and the Dynamic's two buttons only, as the finding's control list says. The GM can still delete the card from the chat log, so 'no button can close it' is literal but not 'nothing can'; minor holds.

checked.claim: The notice history's list holds a change to drawn entries while focus is inside it, until focus leaves, and puts new entries behind a pill while scrolled or focused
checked.why: changed() sets stale and does not redraw while focus is in the list (notice-history-app.mjs:363-378); the focusout listener redraws once focus leaves (304-307). The wait is wider than keepLive's rule 1: it is any focus in the list, not a text field (a summary focused by the click that opened an entry is enough), and there is no field in the list to keep. The reader filed it nit as a recorded A7 design (comment at 357-362); D-A1 (DECISIONS.md, 20.11.2026) is the owner's later call on exactly this kind of wait-for-focus and says a surface still on it is a major finding. The severity is raised for that rule, not for its table cost, which is small.
